chunks: If a man dies and leaves behind two parents, a wife, and a son, then the wife has one-eighth, the two parents have the two sixths, and whatever remains belongs to the son. Likewise, if there are two sons, or three sons, or more than that, they only have whatever remains.

If he leaves behind a wife, two parents, and a daughter, then the wife has one-eighth, the two parents have the two sixths, and the daughter has one-half. Whatever remains is returned to the daughter and the two parents in proportion to their shares, and nothing is returned to the wife nor to the husband.

And this is out of twenty-four, because of the presence of one-eighth. When one-eighth, the two sixths, and one-half are taken from it, one share remains, but it does not divide evenly among five, so five is multiplied by twenty-four, making one hundred and twenty. The wife has one-eighth of that, which is fifteen; the two parents have the two sixths of that, which is forty; and sixty-five remain. The daughter has one-half of that, which is sixty; then five remain, of which three go to the daughter, so that in her hand there become sixty-three, and two of that go to the two parents, so that in their hands there become forty-two.

Likewise, if a man dies and leaves behind a wife, two daughters or more than that, and two parents, then the wife has one-eighth, the two parents have the two sixths, and whatever remains belongs to the daughters. And al-'awl is invalid in this case, because if the daughters had been sons, they would have had only whatever remained.

key_terms.السُّدُسَانِ: the combined two sixths assigned to the two parents
key_terms.النِّصْفُ: one-half share assigned to the daughter
key_terms.الْعَوْلُ: the doctrine of proportionally reducing shares when they exceed the estate; rejected here
key_terms.رُدَّ عَلَى الِابْنَةِ وَالْأَبَوَيْنِ: the remainder is returned to the daughter and the parents proportionally

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance divided between a wife, parents, sons, and daughters in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out inheritance rulings for cases in which a deceased man leaves a wife, parents, and children. It explains the fixed shares, the return of any remainder to certain heirs in proportion to their shares, and rejects al-'awl in the case discussed.
